title: Directions, Turns and Three-Figure Bearings
seo_title: Bearings and Directions – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify the eight points of the compass; measure turns in degrees; give and use three-figure bearings; find back bearings. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on directions and bearings: the eight compass points, turning through angles, three-figure bearings and back bearings. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Bearings start at north and go clockwise
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The four main points are north, east, south and west. Between them are north-east, south-east, south-west and north-west.
  • A bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north. It is written with three figures: east is 090°.
  • The back bearing is the bearing for the return journey: add 180° if the bearing is less than 180°, otherwise subtract 180°.

Examples

Example

Bearing of south-west

South is 180°, south-west is 45° more

Answer: 225°

Example

Back bearing of 070°

70 + 180

Answer: 250°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Measuring anticlockwiseBearings always go clockwise from north.
Writing 45° instead of 045°A bearing has three figures.
Forgetting the 180° for the way backBack bearing = bearing ± 180°.

items.q: Ife is facing West. She makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
items.e: Turn clockwise N → E → S → W. A quarter turn anticlockwise from West gives South.

items.q: Nonso is facing North. He makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
